title: Shadow Deployment Evaluation Playbook for Private & Dedicated Environments
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines the standard process and acceptance criteria for "shadow" (non-traffic, mirrored) evaluation deployments of new model builds and quantized model variants in Redwood Private and Dedicated environments. Shadow deployment is intended to provide realistic, safety-aware, and cost-conscious validation without exposing production traffic to unvetted model behavior.

Goals:
- Detect functional regressions and quality drift early when promoting model builds to Dedicated or Private customer pools.
- Verify quantization/3rd-party compilation impacts under representative workload shapes.
- Validate operational metrics (latency p50/p95, memory pressure, KV cache hit distribution) in the target deployment topology.
- Produce deterministic promotion signals for canary/fallback policies in the Redwood Console.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: model promotions intended for Dedicated pools and Private (VPC/on-prem) installs that will be pinned or exposed to customer traffic.
- Not intended for hosted-only experimentation (use hosted eval harness).

Key definitions:
- Shadow deployment: A deployment that receives a copy of production-like requests (via sampling or replay) but does not return responses to end users.
- Evaluation cohort: A configured set of prompts, demographic slices, and synthetic adversarial cases used during the shadow period.
- Quantization variant: Any model build with reduced precision or kernel-level compilation differences (int8, bfloat16, fq4) intended to lower unit costs.

Prerequisites:
1. Model build has passed unit and integration tests and a baseline acceptance in the central eval harness (see related eval-harness matrix).
2. Target Dedicated/Private environment is provisioned with matching runtime version and kernel profiles.
3. Baseline production telemetry snapshot captured (last 7 days) for comparison.
4. Owner, SRE, and customer (if applicable) sign-off on shadow window and data collection.

Evaluation inputs (test sets & strategies):
- Live-sampled traffic (1-5% of production routed to shadow) OR replayed request traces from the last 72 hours.
- Seeded prompt set: 500 in-distribution prompts representative of heavy-usage features (summarization, instruction-following, extraction).
- Robustness seed: 200 adversarial/noise prompts (typo/obfuscation, ambiguous instructions).
- Long-context stress: 100 prompts with >8k token context to exercise KV cache and attention kernels.
- Safety vectors: 250 safety-sensitive prompts focusing on policy and hallucination triggers.
- Quant-sensitivity partition: the above seed sets with token lengths and shot counts sampled to match expected CTA distributions.

Evaluation metrics and thresholds (promotion-oriented):
- Quality: semantic-similarity-based regression <= 5% drop relative to baseline on the seed test set (metric: pairwise BLEU/ROUGE + embedding cosine > 0.88 for key tasks).
- Safety: no new high-risk safety failures (severity >= 4) introduced; critical safety count must be zero.
- Latency: p50 delta <= +10ms, p95 delta <= +40ms relative to baseline.
- Memory: peak GPU memory <= baseline + 5% for Dedicated; for Private, must meet node capacity headroom >= 10%.
- KV cache behavior: cache hit-rate change <= 3 percentage points; cold-start token overhead <= 12%.
- Regression triage score: composite (quality, safety, perf) must be green for automated promotion. See scoring formula below.

Composite regression triage score (used to decide automated gating):
- Quality (50%), Safety (30%), Latency & Memory combined (20%).
- Score mapping: Green >= 90, Yellow 70-90 (manual review), Red < 70 (reject).

Shadow deployment configuration example (table as plain text):
- runtime_version: 2.14.0
- model_variant: my-model-v3-quant-fq4
- routing_mode: mirror (no user-facing responses)
- traffic_sample: 0.02  # 2% of production requests
- replay_window: 72h
- eval_window: 48h
- data_retention_for_debug: 30d
- telemetry_enabled: true (tokens, delta-logs, raw-outputs hashed)

Procedure (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (Day -3 to -1)
   - a) Create shadow deployment config in Redwood Console with owner, SLOs, and telemetry toggles.
   - b) Register evaluation cohort (IDs for seed prompt sets, adversarial cases, long-context suite).
   - c) Capture production baseline metrics snapshot (p50/p95 latencies, token cost per request, KV cache distribution).
   - d) Notify SRE and customer success of shadow start time and debug contact.
2) Launch & warm-up (Day 0)
   - a) Start shadow at 0.1% traffic-sample using mirror routing for 2 hours to validate no impact on production.
   - b) Validate telemetry ingestion (token-level breakdowns, kernel selection tags, memory traces).
   - c) Escalate and rollback if initial memory or latency anomalies exceed thresholds (see rollback criteria).
3) Full shadow evaluation (Day 0–2)
   - a) Ramp to target sampling rate (e.g., 2%).
   - b) Run scheduled seeded tests (nightly regression suite) and continuous adversarial stream.
   - c) Run quant-sensitivity comparisons: run paired inference for float vs quant variant on matched requests to compute per-request delta metrics.
4) Analysis (Day 2–3)
   - a) Produce evaluation report summarizing quality, safety, perf, and regression triage score.
   - b) If Yellow, schedule manual triage with ML owner, SRE, and Safety SME; for Red, block promotion and open a regression ticket.
5) Promotion decision (Day 3+)
   - a) If Green, proceed to canary traffic rollout as defined in the canary promotion playbook.
   - b) If manual remediation required, iterate on model or runtime config and re-run shadow.

Rollback criteria (immediate or automated):
- Any critical safety failure (severity >= 4) observed in the shadow outputs.
- Sustained p95 latency exceeding baseline + 100ms for >10 minutes.
- GPU memory OOM or >95% sustained memory utilization for >5 minutes.
- KV cache churn leading to cold-start amplification >25% over baseline.

Triage and debugging playbook (on Yellow/Red):
- Ownership: ML owner to lead quality triage; SRE to lead perf/memory; Safety SME to lead policy incidents.
- Minimum artifact set to open triage ticket: failing request IDs, model build hash, runtime kernel tags, quant config, and raw model output (hashed + redacted as needed).
- Standard steps: reproduce failure with isolated replay; narrow to minimal prompt; compare float vs quantized outputs; run profiler to capture kernel-level hot paths.

Privacy and telemetry controls:
- Shadow deployments must respect PII/data retention policies. Raw outputs used for triage must be hashed or redacted before storage.
- Data collected during shadow is governed by the customer-specific confidentiality flag; for Private installs, default to restricted unless customer explicitly permits debug artifact sharing.

Operational knobs and recommendations:
- Use continuous batching profiles tuned for the target pool to avoid spurious latency regressions when sampling traffic.
- Prefer paired inference (float vs candidate) for a statistically robust delta rather than absolute thresholds alone.
- When validating quantized builds, include both microbench kernels and end-to-end user-level prompts in the same shadow window.

Example commands and snippets:
- Create a shadow route (CLI pseudo):
```
redwood route create --env prod-dedicated-eu --model my-model:v3-quant --route-type mirror --sample-rate 0.02 --telemetry on --eval-cohort seedy-2026-01
```
- Run paired inference comparator (local):
```python
# comparator.py (simplified)
from redwood_eval import InferenceClient
client_float = InferenceClient(model='my-model:v3')
client_quant = InferenceClient(model='my-model:v3-quant')
for prompt in prompts:
    a = client_float.generate(prompt)
    b = client_quant.generate(prompt)
    print(prompt.id, embedding_similarity(a,b), latency_delta(a,b))
```

Acceptance report template (deliverable):
- Summary (one-paragraph)
- Baseline vs candidate comparison (table of metrics)
- Regression triage score and breakdown
- Safety findings (counts + examples)
- Perf findings (latency histogram, memory timeline)
- Recommendation: Promote / Remediate / Block (with owners and ETA)

Ownership and SLAs:
- ML owner: create shadow config, interpret quality signals, own remediation.
- SRE owner: validate runtime compatibility, address perf regressions, own rollback.
- Safety/Policy: review any flagged safety cases within 24 hours.
- SLA for shadow evaluations: evaluations should finish and a report be produced within 72 hours of shadow launch for standard promotions.

Appendix: quick checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Register evaluation cohort
- [ ] Capture baseline telemetry
- [ ] Create shadow route with mirror routing
- [ ] Run warm-up and validate telemetry
- [ ] Ramp to target sampling and run seed/adversarial sets
- [ ] Run paired float-vs-quant comparisons
- [ ] Produce acceptance report
- [ ] Decision: Promote / Remediate / Block

This playbook should be updated annually or whenever changes are made to the runtime (kernel selection, batching model) or the promotion scoring formula. For questions or exceptions, contact the playbook owner (Maya Chen) or SRE lead (Alejandro Ruiz).
